probe.note: Five neutral probe solves (weighted sum, no floors) of the actual design problem; values are achieved, feasible designs. Ranges are indicative, not exhaustive.

justification.normalisation: Runtime is bounded by the physical 41-62.5 h envelope, siren and voice use the probe-achieved ranges (2.0-3.2 h, 70-90 SII), and L5 spans 0.05-0.30 to cover the probe range of 0.073-0.267 without flattering any objective.
justification.scalarisation: Achievement (Tchebycheff) is chosen because the probes show a sharp runtime-vs-L5 trade (62.3 h/0.092 vs 45.2 h/0.267) that a weighted sum could miss on non-convex segments.
justification.aspiration: Each target sits at or just above a single-probe achievement (runtime 62.3 h, siren 3.14 h, voice 77.7, L5 0.267), with L5 at 0.25 and runtime at the 60 h marketing goal, so every aspiration is reachable individually and the solver only has to find the joint compromise.
justification.objective_floors: Siren endurance of at least 3 hours at 86 dB @ 1 m is a stated program requirement, and every probe that met it (3.14 h at best) was feasible, so it is a hard floor; runtime (marketing ~60 h), voice and L5 are goals rather than requirements and are left unfloored.
justification.weights: Runtime carries the most weight (0.35) because ~60 h is the headline marketing target, L5 (0.25) is weighted for the 'strong GNSS' goal given its wide achievable spread, and siren and voice share 0.20 each since siren is already protected by its floor.
